heard: Great white sharks don't actually want to eat you. For many decades, Hollywood movies and popular novels cemented the great white shark as a relentless man-eater. Marine scientists explain that most recorded bites are actually exploratory investigations by curious animals. When encountering an unfamiliar object like a surfboard, the massive apex predator takes a careful test bite. It uses flexible tooth beds and sensitive jaws to gather tactile evidence and figure out what is floating there. Because human bodies are much too bony and completely lack high-fat blubber, sharks almost always spit a straight back out. Extensive research proves that great white sharks don't actually want to eat you.
